analysis: Examined three changed files. (1) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift lines 304-310: after the preload summary, the driver enqueues selected-model recovery for models skipped for memory, failed for memory, or not attempted. This is guarded by !Task.isCancelled, !isShuttingDown and !startupPreloadStopRequested. The recovery implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery) is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify that its load uses allowEviction:false, honors servingDrain/add-on hold (TB-012, T-059), or respects the retirement tombstones and failedSelfTestHashes. Those are integration questions, not findings. (2) ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift lines 61-108: unloadAllModelsForShutdown replaces the unbounded unload loop with a per-slot 15s bounded wait. Slots whose unload does not finish are abandoned and logged, and process exit reclaims the memory. This improves availability (T-010/T-029 class) and does not widen the plaintext exposure surface. Residual consideration: abandoned slots could leave decrypted KV/GPU data (T-028) in memory until process exit. Process exit is imminent and the memory is not reachable by consumers, so I did not treat this as a regression. The ShutdownUnloadFlag uses an NSLock and is thread-safe. The unstructured Task { unloadModel } can outlive the wait, which is intended. coordinatorClient shutdown and the drain occur before the unloads, as in the base. Power assertions are released after the unloads regardless of abandonment. (3) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift lines 514-525: only test seams are added (selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride and an await on the recovery attempt). These are internal-level and are not production-reachable beyond @testable use. No changes touch the wire protocol, keys, attestation, cache encryption (T-041), or the authorization boundaries. Needs deeper review only of the unseen SelectedModelRecovery file.
